- Overestimate early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days; undercorrect for initial spikes.
- Underestimate during sharp upward trends; model tends to lag behind actual price momentum.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 60→70 range); model overreacts and peaks too early.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds too high a mean in the middle of the horizon; true values revert to lower levels later.
- Forecast horizon 10–15 days: model consistently underestimates true values; adjust upward by 1–2% for this window.
- Late horizon (20–30 days): model tends to overestimate; apply downward correction of 1–3% for final 5–10 days.
- Avoid “smooth” forecasts; model underreacts to volatility; add volatility-weighted adjustment for high-std periods.
